text_blocks.snippet:
thought
Losartan (Cozaar) is an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) used to treat high blood pressure, protect kidney function in type 2 diabetes, and reduce stroke risk. While generally well-tolerated, it can cause several side effects.

list.snippet: Dizziness or lightheadedness (especially when standing up quickly due to a drop in blood pressure)
Upper respiratory tract infections or nasal congestion
Back or joint pain and muscle cramps
Digestive issues such as nausea, diarrhea, or mild stomach upset
Dry cough (less common with ARBs than with ACE inhibitors, but still possible)
Low blood pressure (hypotension): Can cause fainting, severe dizziness, or blurry vision.
High potassium levels (hyperkalemia): Can lead to muscle weakness, slow or irregular heartbeat, and heart palpitations.
Kidney function changes or acute kidney injury: May show up as changes in the amount or appearance of urine or swelling in the hands, ankles, or feet.
Allergic reactions (angioedema): Potentially life-threatening swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or trouble breathing/swallowing.
Fetal toxicity: Losartan must not be used during pregnancy as it can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby.
